Reasoning: Initially the two balls carry unlike charges, so they attract each other. Let the initial distance between the two balls be r, then the magnitude of the initial Coulomb force is F0 = k|8q·(-2q)|/r^2 = 16kq^2/r^2. The two balls have the same mass, so the magnitude of the initial acceleration is proportional to this force. When the two balls touch, because they are identical metal balls, the total charge is 8q - 2q = 6q; after contact it is distributed equally, and each ball carries charge 3q. When the small balls return to their original positions, the distance between the two balls is again equal to the initial distance r; at this time both balls carry 3q, and the magnitude of the Coulomb force is F = k(3q)(3q)/r^2 = 9kq^2/r^2. The mass is unchanged, so the ratio of the accelerations is F/F0 = 9/16.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as two identical metal spheres A and B resting on the same insulated horizontal surface, with A initially to the left of B. From the text, take their initial charges as 8q and -2q and note that the surface is smooth, so horizontal acceleration is only due to electrostatic force. Since the opposite charges attract, the identical conducting spheres eventually touch; on contact, total charge 8q - 2q = 6q is shared equally, so each sphere becomes charged 3q. When a sphere returns to its original position, the diagram/text imply the separation between the two original positions is again the initial separation r. Compare Coulomb accelerations at the same separation: initially F0 = k|8q·(-2q)|/r^2 = 16kq^2/r^2, later F = k(3q)(3q)/r^2 = 9kq^2/r^2. With identical masses, the acceleration ratio is F/F0 = 9/16.
